Investigating now — preliminary findings from the edge and runtime traces:

- Symptom: p95/p99 latency spike and 5xxs correlate with burst windows where a small fraction (~6%) of requests have very large context (>>16k tokens) and trigger long KV prefetches.
- Root cause signal: observed frequent KV cache evictions on tenant shard "cleardata-10" and heavy head-of-line blocking inside the default batch lane. Long requests stall assembling batches, blocking many small/fast requests behind them.
- Key evidence: hotkey log excerpts (attached: hotkey-sample-logs.txt) show contiguous eviction cycles and cache miss storms; kernel-level timelines show lanes stalling for ~900–1400ms on prefetch ops.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (can be applied without model changes):
1) Toggle hot-request bypass for this tenant (bypass long-context requests to their dedicated lane) — reduces HOL for small requests.
2) Reduce default max_batch_latency from 20ms -> 8ms for the affected pool.
3) Increase KV cache capacity for "cleardata-10" shard by 30% (pin a higher reservation) and bump eviction_threshold to 0.85 to avoid churning from prefetch surges.
4) Deploy a temporary prefetch rate-limit: max_concurrent_prefetch per worker = 8 (was 32).

Risks: cache capacity change requires brief rolling restart of the pool (no model load/unload) — ~6–8 mins per pod, rolling across 6 pods => estimated 45 mins if sequential. The bypass + batch latency reduction are config flags that can be toggled live with <2 min impact.

I'm attaching p99-latency-breakdown.csv and the log snippet. Will run an A/B test on 2 nodes with bypass + batch window reduction and report back.

- Rishi (SRE)

Update and confirmation:

- Canaries (hot-request-bypass + max_batch_latency=8ms) were enabled on 2 nodes at 09:28 UTC. Within 10 minutes we saw p99 reduce from ~1.9s -> ~510ms and 5xxs drop to 0.6%.
- We completed a measured roll (wave 1/3) and metrics remained stable. We are pausing further waves to prepare a controlled cache-reservation bump (non-disruptive planned at 23:00 PST) to fully remove eviction churn.
- Post-action artifacts: attached latency CSV and hotkey logs. We opened INF-9876 for follow-up (long-term: tenant-level cache isolation, per-request prefetch prioritization, and a guardrail that demotes very long-context requests to an isolated lane).

Next steps:
- Marissa will coordinate a short maintenance authorization with ClearData for the 23:00 PST slot.
- Rishi will own the post-incident follow-up and produce a short RCA by 2026-12-03.
- Soojin to escalate request for a one-time SLA credit evaluation to Accounts (copying Billing thread).
